To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The probability that a firm is short term credit ration is higher with banks with trading abilities.

(i) the probability of being shortterm credit rationed is significantly lower for firms that are more financially constrained; (ii) this effect is larger for firms that borrow more frequently and for firms that borrow in the short term; (iii) the probability of short term credit rationning is significantly higher for firms that borrow from banks that are more likely to be short-term constrained.
The probability of being short-term credit rationed is lower with banks that exhibit non-trading abilities.
